title: Blood pressure per visit
prompt: A nurse reviewing blood pressure wants the two readings as plain columns. Write `solve(encounters)` so it returns each visit's `encounter_id`, `patient_id`, `systolic` and `diastolic`.
rules: Return four columns, in this order: `encounter_id`, `patient_id`, `systolic`, `diastolic`.
`systolic` and `diastolic` are the fields of the same names inside `vitals`, unchanged.
Keep every visit, duplicates included. A visit with no vitals has both readings missing.
hints: `vitals` is a struct. A field inside it is written `"vitals.systolic"`.
The dot form names the result after the field, so no `alias` is needed.
With brackets, `F.col("vitals")["systolic"]` is named `vitals.systolic` until you add `.alias("systolic")`.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(encounters):
    # encounter_id, patient_id, systolic, diastolic
    return encounters
explanation: Name the fields with a dot: `encounters.select("encounter_id", "patient_id", "vitals.systolic", "vitals.diastolic")`. The dot form names each result after its field. `F.col("vitals")["systolic"].alias("systolic")` gives the same column; without the `alias` it is called `vitals.systolic`, which is the usual slip. A video visit has no vitals at all, and reading a field from a missing struct gives a missing value, so nothing special is needed for those rows.
